name: Siltmoth Canteen — Shelf Ferment Kitchen
creator: Adaora Nkemdirim-Vasquez
description: A Tier 1 walk-up canteen operating out of a reclaimed water-treatment alcove in the Shelf's Ward Fourteen, Siltmoth built its reputation on long-fermented synth-protein pastes aged in repurposed BCI coolant drums — a technique Adaora Nkemdirim-Vasquez developed after losing access to refrigeration for eight months during the 2208 grid failures. The menu cycles weekly and is written in chalk on stripped cable conduit: anchored by a rotating 'funk bowl' of miso-adjacent synth-paste over cracked sorghum, topped with whatever foraged or diverted real-ingredient garnish Nkemdirim-Vasquez can source, typically running Φ4–Φ7 per portion. A second item, the 'cold vinegar broth' — a clear, aggressively sour liquid served in repurposed pharmaceutical vials — became something of a cult object after a food archivist from the Tier 3 Meridian Synthesis Group wrote an unauthorized neural-feed piece about it in 2213.
medium: physical — walk-up counter service, chalk menu board, no neural feed presence
cultural_impact: Siltmoth became shorthand in Shelf food culture for the argument that constraint produces depth — that the fermentation techniques born from grid failure and supply scarcity produced flavor complexity that no licensed synth-cuisine lab had managed to replicate with full resources. The canteen is cited in at least three unauthorized food-archive neural feeds as evidence that the Shelf's culinary underground is not compensating for scarcity but actively transforming it.
controversy: A 2214 licensing inspection by HelixCorp's Municipal Food Safety Division cited Siltmoth for operating without a fermentation permit and using non-certified aging vessels; Nkemdirim-Vasquez paid a Φ200 fine and continued operating unchanged. A subsequent Tier 4 food journalist published a piece called 'The Shelf's Best Restaurant' which drove a brief wave of slum-tourism foot traffic that the local Ward Fourteen community responded to with enough hostility that the journalist required a private transport home. Nkemdirim-Vasquez has publicly stated she does not want Tier 4 coverage and has refused three buyout approaches from Axiom's hospitality licensing arm.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 food archivist who wrote the piece that accidentally triggered slum-tourism returns to Siltmoth in 2216, hoping to apologize — but finds Nkemdirim-Vasquez has disappeared, and the canteen is being run by a rotating collective of Ward Fourteen residents who may or may not know where she went.

Axiom's hospitality licensing arm makes a fourth buyout approach, this time not through paperwork but through a local fixer who begins quietly pressuring Siltmoth's ingredient suppliers — forcing the canteen's regulars to decide how far they're willing to go to keep the place open.

The cold vinegar broth, it turns out, has a secondary effect: the specific bacterial culture Nkemdirim-Vasquez cultivated in the BCI coolant drums produces a mild, short-duration neural clarity effect in people with standard BCI implants — something she either doesn't know about or hasn't disclosed, and which a HelixCorp biochemist has just noticed in routine consumption data.
